manifest_vkeys.note: offline manifest key(s); the TUF root rule -- the root of trust is the least-used key. Successor manifests are valid only with threshold signatures under BOTH the predecessor's and their own key set (for version 1 the log key stands in, as it was version 1's only key).

algorithms.note: ed25519 is the authenticating algorithm; additive post-quantum cosignatures may appear on checkpoints and are not required for quorum

rotation_rule: a successor manifest MUST have version exactly one greater than this one, MUST carry previous_manifest_sha256 equal to the sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonicalization of this manifest without its signatures field, MUST carry signatures meeting the manifest_vkeys threshold of BOTH this manifest and itself, MUST appear at https://markovianprotocol.com/.well-known/trust-root/<version>.json, and its unsigned digest MUST be appended to the log as a trust-root-manifest/v1 leaf covered by a checkpoint cosigned by at least witness_quorum listed witnesses. Clients walk forward one version at a time and check expiry ONLY on the final manifest; an expired final manifest is a hard failure, including a pinned copy. If log_vkeys change between manifests, clients MUST discard cached checkpoints. Log key rotation is valid only if recorded in-log as a log-key-rotation/v1 leaf; revocation as log-key-revocation/v1. Past the manifest_vkeys threshold, recovery is out-of-band.

publication.log_leaf: the sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonicalization of this manifest WITHOUT the signatures field is appended to the log as a trust-root-manifest/v1 leaf; 2.json.leaf is an untrusted index hint, verified via inclusion proof

signatures.signed_over: RFC 8785 canonicalization of the manifest without the signatures field
